newsitem.title: FRANCE: FRENCH GOVERNMENT BACKS RENAULT CHIEF.
newsitem.headline: FRENCH GOVERNMENT BACKS RENAULT CHIEF.

text.p: French Industry Minister Franck Borotra said on Wednesday he supported embattled Renault chairman Louis Schweitzer but responsibility for the decision to axe jobs in Belgium and France lay with the car maker alone.
Several hundred of the company's Belgian employees, facing redundancy in July, drove to France early on Wednesday aboard 20 buses to picket a Renault factory at Douai, south of Lille.
French trade unions declared solidarity with their Belgian comrades.

In a radio interview Borotra acknowledged for the first time Renault had informed the French and Belgian governments of its decision to close the Vilvoorde plant near Brussels a few days before the official announcement was made last Thursday.
His comment appeared to contradict a parliamentary answer he gave on Tuesday in which he said the French authorities had been neither informed nor consulted in advance.
"The chairman of Renault takes responsibility for his decision," Borotra told Europe 1 radio. "I am not abandoning Schweitzer nor the Renault company."
The decision to close Vilvoorde, with the loss of 3,100 direct jobs, was necessary to reduce costs and respond to competition, the minister said.
"Restructurings cannot be avoided," he said, adding "even Renault can die".
But he also said the company had an obligation to limit the human cost of its reorganisation to a minimum.
Borotra said Schweitzer had come to see him a few days before the Vilvoorde decision was announced, followed by more than 2,700 job cuts in France.
"I told him -- you take your responsibility and as a shareholder I will judge your policy by its results," he said.
Asked if Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene, who has bitterly attacked the Renault move, was informed in advance, Borotra said: "Of course, in the days before the announcement."
The Belgian government dramatised its displeasure on Tuesday night by cancelling an order for 150 Renault cars.
Interior Minister Johan Vande Lanotte announced the decision on RTBF radio amid calls by Belgian tabloid newspapers for a boycott of Renault cars.
